experiments.name: address dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 250 --unroll2 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r22, 8; st.d $r22, $r20, 0; li.d $r22, -8; st.d $r22, $r20, 8' --asm 'llacq.d $r4, $r20, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: rj -> rd chain: the address alternates between two words so the load data drives the next address; the add.d is subtracted. The acquiring form is much slower than plain LL: 20 cycles on average (20-21 measured).

latencies.notes: rj -> rd chain: the address alternates between two words so the load data drives the next address; the add.d is subtracted. The acquiring form is much slower than plain LL: 20 cycles on average (20-21 measured).

throughput.name: 8 independent addresses
throughput.asm: llacq.d $r12, $r21; llacq.d $r13, $r23; llacq.d $r14, $r24; llacq.d $r15, $r25; llacq.d $r16, $r26; llacq.d $r17, $r27; llacq.d $r18, $r28; llacq.d $r19, $r29
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --counter 0xa8 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56' --asm 'llacq.d $r12, $r21; llacq.d $r13, $r23; llacq.d $r14, $r24; llacq.d $r15, $r25; llacq.d $r16, $r26; llacq.d $r17, $r27; llacq.d $r18, $r28; llacq.d $r19, $r29'
throughput.notes: 8 atomic memory operations take 168.00 cycles. Extra counters per instruction (normalized by 8 lanes): 0xa8=1.00.

notes: L1D-hit load-linked. Address-to-result latency 20 cycles; the monitor bookkeeping makes it much slower than a plain load (4 cycles).
